ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior officers against the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) PEP list, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, and the New Zealand Sanctions Regime (including the Russia Sanctions Act 2022). Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any PEP, including family members and close associates, with source of wealth and source of funds verification. Continuous monitoring via automated screening tools is mandatory, with immediate reporting of any matches to the FIU under Section 40 of the AML/CFT Act. The screening must cover all jurisdictions where the entity operates, and must be repeated at least annually or upon any material change in ownership or control.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Name Reservation Portal (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English or Maori, or a combination thereof. Names may include numerals, punctuation, and symbols as permitted by the Companies Act 1993. Transliteration is not required, but if a name is in a non-Latin script, it must be transliterated into Latin characters for registration. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or reserved name. The four-tier naming convention includes: (1) the legal element (e.g., 'Limited' or 'Ltd'), (2) the distinctive element, (3) the descriptive element, and (4) any optional geographical or other qualifiers. The name must not imply a connection with the Crown, a government department, or any regulated profession without prior approval.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993, sections 7, 10, 12-21, 26, 30-38, 39-44, 60-69, 83-89 and Schedule 3 (Default Constitution); Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, sections 7-12; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, sections 5, 12, 15, 31, 49 and 56.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Companies Register, Wellington.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZCN1 - Application for Registration of a Limited Company, filed electronically via the Companies Register online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a New Zealand limited liability company. Shares may be issued for nil par value consideration; capital amounts are determined by the directors and recorded in the company register. No escrow account or capital deposit is mandated under the Companies Act 1993. However, the electronic money institution must maintain prudential reserve assets equivalent to 100 percent of its outstanding e-money liabilities at all times as a condition of its Reserve Bank licensing framework.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE SUBSCRIBER DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED PURSUANT TO THE COMPANIES ACT 1993. RESOLVED THAT: 1. The subscribers unconditionally subscribe for and take up the shares in the share capital of the Company as recorded in the Register of Members, and the Board is authorised to allot and issue such shares to the persons named therein upon the terms of the adopted constitution. 2. The constitution tabled at this meeting is approved and adopted and shall bind the Company and all members in accordance with section 26 of the Companies Act 1993. 3. The registered office of the Company shall be established and maintained at the physical address notified to the Companies Office, and any relocation shall be filed with the Registrar in accordance with section 188. 4. The following persons are appointed as the first directors of the Company: [NAME], [NAME] and [NAME], each having executed a consent to act as director under section 151. 5. The directors are authorised to open bank accounts with a registered New Zealand bank, to obtain registration with Inland Revenue for income tax and goods and services tax, and to engage licensed counsel for the company's financial service provider registration and electronic money institution licence applications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register Online Portal (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an electronic name availability search on the Companies Register. Reserve an approved company name that is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing name and that is not offensive or misleading under section 20 of the Companies Act 1993. For a licensed electronic money institution, the name must not contain the word 'bank', 'trust' or 'insurance' without the prior written consent of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand or the Financial Markets Authority. Submit a name reservation through the portal and retain the reservation confirmation reference.
required_dossiers: Explanation of business purpose if name includes regulated terms
Letters of no objection from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand or Financial Markets Authority if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused under section 20, submit a revised application with an alternative name, or file a written submission to the Registrar demonstrating that the name is not misleading. A further statutory review may be sought in the High Court under section 25.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitution Adoption and Corporate Governance Instrumentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Subscriber Directors and/or Founding Shareholders of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt a bespoke constitution or expressly elect to apply the default rules in Schedule 3 of the Companies Act 1993. Prepare and execute consent to act forms for each director, minutes of the subscriber meeting, a share register, and a register of ultimate beneficial owners under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) requirements. Where institutional investors are anticipated, include enhanced reserved matter provisions, board quorum rules, and procedures for conflicts of interest under sections 140 to 144. Finalize the registered office address and the address for service in New Zealand.
required_dossiers: Written consents to act as director of all proposed directors
Minutes of the subscriber shareholders' meeting
Registered office and address for service declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any constitutional provision conflicts with the Companies Act 1993, the Act prevails and the provision is void to the extent of the inconsistency. Cure by passing a special resolution to amend the constitution and re-filing the amended document.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Filing with the Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Electronically file Form NZCN1 through the Companies Register online portal. Provide the approved company name, the registered office physical address, the director details (including address, birth date, and identification), the intended share structure with classes and rights attaching, the total number of shares, and the names and addresses of the shareholders. Pay the statutory filing fee of NZD 105.40 by credit card or direct debit. Upload the executed consents to act. Upon approval, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation and an automatic New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). The entity is then deemed to be a legal person with limited liability.
required_dossiers: Consents to act for all directors
Proof of identity for each director (passport or national identity document)
Proof of residential address for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of defect under section 26 of the Companies Act 1993, the applicant has 20 working days to rectify the specified omissions. If the application lapses, a fresh application must be filed with payment of a new fee. Judicial review is available for an unreasonable refusal to register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Tax Registration and NZBN Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) and NZBN Registry, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with Inland Revenue for income tax purposes using the issued NZBN. Obtain a New Zealand IRD number. Register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) at the standard rate of 15 percent if the projected annual taxable turnover equals or exceeds NZD 60,000 or if the company intends to claim input credits. Register as an employer for PAYE, ACC (Accident Compensation Corporation) and KiwiSaver if employees will be engaged. Enrol for MyIR online services and confirm the overseas or local director IRD numbers.
required_dossiers: Projected revenue and GST registration declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD queries the application because of incomplete overseas director information, provide certified passport copies and obtain IRD numbers for the non-resident directors before finalising the registration. Penalties for late GST registration are remitted if voluntary disclosure is made prior to assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Financial Service Providers (operated by the Companies Office, MBIE, under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online FSP application through the Financial Service Providers Register portal. Select the applicable financial service categories: (a) issuing electronic money; (b) payment and money remittance services; and (c) custodial and reserve management services. Join an approved dispute resolution scheme, preferably the Financial Services Complaints Limited (FSCL), and obtain an FSPR registration number. Disclose all directors, ultimate beneficial owners, and any adverse regulatory history. Ensure the registration is completed before offering any financial service to customers in New Zealand.
required_dossiers: Director and beneficial owner disclosure forms
Details of financial services to be provided
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar proposes to refuse registration on the ground that registration is not in the public interest, the company may make written representations within the statutory response period and may seek a review by the Financial Markets Authority. If the dispute resolution scheme membership lapses, a substitute scheme must be joined immediately to avoid deregistration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: AML/CFT Reporting Entity Registration and Compliance Programme Implementation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Internal Affairs (DIA), AML/CFT Group, and Reserve Bank of New Zealand for prudential supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as a reporting entity under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. Prepare and adopt a written AML/CFT compliance programme that includes a business risk assessment, customer due diligence procedures, enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons and high-risk jurisdictions, suspicious transaction reporting procedures, mandatory staff training schedules, and independent audit requirements. Appoint a designated AML/CFT compliance officer at senior management level. File the compliance programme and the appointment notice with the appropriate supervisor, which for an electronic money institution is the Department of Internal Affairs unless a banking licence is held, in which case the Reserve Bank of New Zealand is the AML/CFT supervisor.
required_dossiers: Appointment letter of the AML/CFT compliance officer
Sanctions screening and transaction monitoring procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the supervisor raises a concern under section 80 of the AML/CFT Act, the entity must promptly remediate the deficiency and provide a written corrective action plan. Failure to comply may result in a formal warning, an enforceable undertaking, or civil penalty proceedings; the company may appeal such decisions to the High Court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand, Prudential Supervision Department
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Electronic Money Institution Licence for Virtual IBAN Issuance and Digital Wallet Reserve Management, issued under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021 and the Banking Prudential Supervision framework, together with Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) authorisation and AML/CFT reporting entity registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) of New Zealand, in coordination with the territorial local authority acting as Building Consent Authority under the Building Act 2004
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 5 - Exempt (pure office-based digital financial services). No mandatory full Environmental Impact Assessment or Notice of Requirement is required under Schedule 4 of the Resource Management Act 1991 for Virtual IBAN issuance, digital wallet administration or reserve management activities conducted in a leased office, because no land disturbance, manufacturing, or discharge to land or water is involved. The activity is consistent with permitted administrative office use under applicable district plan zoning.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Emissions: no stationary sources; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions are limited to negligible office cleaning and IT equipment usage, subject to the ambient air quality standards under the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards for Air Quality) Regulations 2004. Wastewater: office sanitary discharge is permitted through the territorial local authority municipal network and must comply with the local Trade Waste Bylaw if any pre-treatment is required. Waste: e-waste from IT infrastructure must be disposed of through a certified e-waste recycler in accordance with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and the Hazardous Substances (Disposal) Notice 2017. Any backup diesel generator, if installed, must comply with the National Environmental Standard for Air Quality emission limits for stationary combustion engines.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake) — administered through the myIR online portal at https://www.ird.govt.nz.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A New Zealand limited company is first incorporated in the Companies Office, which issues the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) and normally auto-populates the Inland Revenue number through the integrated Companies Office/IRD business transformation registration process. If the IRD number is not automatically issued, the company must submit Form IRD 596 (Application for an IRD number for a New Zealand company) or register via myIR. Foreign beneficial owners require a New Zealand registered office and resident agent address for Companies Office purposes; the same address is used for IRD correspondence. Following IRD number allocation, the company must separately register for GST in myIR (or via the GST 2A application) where annual taxable supplies are expected to exceed NZD 60,000, or elect voluntary registration. The EMI must also obtain the applicable financial services licensing acknowledgement from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand before operating, although this is not a tax registration step.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — New Zealand resident limited companies are taxed at the entity level at 28% corporate income tax on worldwide income; tax losses may be carried forward and imputation credits attach to dividends. A non-resident owned NZ Ltd remains an entity-level taxpayer; distributions to non-residents may attract NRWT or be made under an approved issuer levy. No default flow-through treatment exists, although an eligible closely held company may elect Look-Through Company status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not offer a full check-the-box election. Qualifying closely held companies (five or fewer owners and satisfying statutory restrictions) may elect Look-Through Company (LTC) status under the Income Tax Act 2007, causing income, losses, and credits to be attributed to owners. For cross-border hybrid structures, New Zealand provides the foreign hybrid entity classification regime at sections FA 2-FA 10 and related hybrid mismatch election and notification protocols that permit alignment of entity treatment with foreign jurisdictions. Portfolio Investment Entity (PIE) elections are available only for qualifying managed investment vehicles and are not relevant to a standard trading EMI subsidiary.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, administered by Inland Revenue
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; compulsory registration applies once this turnover threshold is reached or exceeded. Voluntary registration is available below the threshold. Financial supplies such as electronic money and payment services are generally exempt from GST, so an EMI that makes only exempt financial supplies is not required to register for GST; however, registration may be elected to recover input tax where the entity also makes zero-rated exported financial services to non-residents.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), or digital stamping regime applies in New Zealand. New Zealand has adopted the international PEPPOL e-invoicing framework; from 1 April 2022, central government agencies were required to be able to receive electronic invoices using PEPPOL BIS 3.0, and suppliers to government may be contractually obliged to send e-invoices through a PEPPOL access point. There is no IRD-operated invoice clearance API and no mandate for private-sector e-invoicing, although voluntary e-invoicing is supported by the IRD.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for goods under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 requires that the supplier physically exports the goods from New Zealand, usually evidenced by a New Zealand Customs export entry and commercial transport documentation. Zero-rating for offshore services under section 11A is available when the services are supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply and the services are performed outside New Zealand, subject to exceptions where the services are for the direct benefit of an NZ resident. For an Electronic Money Institution (EMI), virtual IBAN issuance, digital wallet reserve management, and payment processing supplied to non-resident corporate clients are zero-rated as offshore financial services only if the recipient is non-resident, the services do not directly benefit a New Zealand resident, and the arrangement is not a GST-avoidance scheme. The EMI must maintain contemporaneous evidence of customer residence status, the offshore purpose of the supply, and the non-NZ deployment of the financial service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (New Zealand Customs Service electronic Export Entry filed through the Trade Single Window and cleared at the port of export)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or other contract of carriage demonstrating physical export from New Zealand
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank SWIFT/MT103 payment evidence for export proceeds where the 180-day FX repatriation directive applies
Export sales contract and commercial invoice clearly describing the exported goods or offshore financial services and the zero-rating basis
Packing list, container/serial numbers, courier delivery confirmation, and foreign customs arrival evidence
Section 11A non-resident declaration forms, customer residence certificates, and officer sign-off for zero-rated financial services supplied to non-residents
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue rigorously scrutinises export zero-rating claims, particularly for financial services supplied to non-residents, requiring the EMI to hold full contemporaneous documentation. If a zero-rating position is reversed, the company becomes retrospectively liable for the GST shortfall, together with use-of-money interest from the original due date. Civil shortfall penalties range from 20% for lack of reasonable care to 150% for intentional evasion or hiding of documents, and late payment interest compounds. Fraudulent export zero-rating or intentional false statements constitute tax evasion offences under sections 143B and 143C of the Tax Administration Act 1994, carrying fines of up to NZD 75,000 for individuals (up to NZD 150,000 for a body corporate) and imprisonment of up to five years for natural persons. Directors and officers who knowingly participate may also face personal liability and disqualification-type enforcement under the Companies Act 1993 and, for licensed EMIs, additional regulatory enforcement by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) — acting as the central bank and operator of the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS), while the Overseas Investment Office (OIO) administers foreign direct investment screening and the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) enforces tax-related remittance compliance; there is no distinct foreign exchange administration office in New Zealand.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) is fully convertible for both current account and capital account transactions. The capital account is liberalized subject to the Overseas Investment Act 2005, which requires consent for non-resident acquisitions of sensitive land, fishing quota, or significant business assets (generally NZD 100 million or more). Profit remittances do not require central bank approval; however, dividend distributions to non-residents are subject to non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) at the treaty applicable rate, and banks may request an IRD certificate or tax clearance for exceptionally large outbound remittances as part of enhanced due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or repatriation timeline exists for export receipts in New Zealand. Exporters and digital wallet operators may retain sale proceeds in any freely convertible foreign currency indefinitely. There is no mandatory conversion ratio. If proceeds are credited to a New Zealand bank account, standard AML/CFT monitoring and IRD reporting obligations apply, and conversion to NZD occurs at prevailing market rates through the wholesale interbank market at no central bank direction.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium — Offshore digital EMIs may operate in New Zealand as registered Money Remitters under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, but they cannot hold NZD-denominated client funds directly and must partner with a locally licensed bank. Such partnerships are feasible but carry heavy compliance requirements, including AML/CFT Act 2009 obligations, restrictions on providing interest-bearing services, and enhanced scrutiny on 'money mule' systems. Viability is stronger for EMIs with a proven licence in an equivalent jurisdiction and a valid registration on the New Zealand Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR).
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: High — For a High_Risk_Special_License entity such as a licensed EMI, the major New Zealand banks mandate a physical meeting or a rigorous, pre-arranged remote video interview with a director and the compliance officer. Remote opening is only permitted where a bank's digital onboarding infrastructure is combined with independently verified identity documents (notarized or apostilled by a certified professional introducer), a local NZ-resident director or professional referrer, and successful enhanced due diligence on all beneficial owners. No full remote onboarding is offered for such entities without an existing long-term banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Structural complexity arising from virtual IBAN issuance and cascading of digital wallet reserves across multiple segregated accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licensed EMI status confirmation issued by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand; reserve management and client-fund segregation deed; documented treasury ledger mapping wallet balances to underlying transaction rails; AML/CFT programme certified in accordance with Financial Markets Authority (FMA) guidelines; name and profile of the appointed Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO); current CYCLAR audit report; a technical white paper that explains virtual IBAN allocation logic and the chain of custody of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO concentration, with over 70% of directors based in China, Hong Kong, or offshore financial centres.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO chain representation up to individuals; notarized and apostilled passport copies for every director and shareholder; independent reference from a New Zealand chartered accountant or practising lawyer confirming the legitimacy of the business; certified source-of-wealth statements covering available liquid assets; the appointment of a New Zealand resident director to provide local governance; valid IRD tax identification numbers and foreign tax residency declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected transaction velocity exceeding NZD 2 million per month without the production of conventional sales or service invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed transaction lifecycle map with counterparty origin data; exclusive use of outward-bound SWIFT MT103 payment rails with complete beneficiary codes (BIC, bank identifier, purpose codes 1013 or 1014); audit trail of source-of-crypto or source-of-wallet funds for all claimed on-chain liquidations; contractual prohibition on handling anonymous e-wallet assets; periodic independent compliance sampling and reporting to the bank's CRO.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital is routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 for large corporate transfers denominated in NZD, USD, or CNY, with purpose codes explicitly detailing 'Capital Injection' or 'Equity Subscription' for foreign direct investment. The receiving New Zealand settlement bank clears the funds via the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) operated by the Reserve Bank, or through a Foreign Currency Settlement Account (FCSA) for non-NZD liquidity. Verification entails SWIFT FIN MT103 acknowledgement (or MT103 RETURN/REJECT acknowledgment), the transacting bank's BIC and the recalling of wire-trace documentation. For a licensed EMI, investor capital must be locked in a capital escrow account until evidence of VAT/IRD classification, source-of-funds diligence and corporate extraction ratification is filed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and settlement disbursements fire over SWIFT MT103 for high-speed correspondent transfers, using the SWIFT gpi tracking service for end-to-end status monitoring. For documentary trade settlement, a Commercial Letter of Credit is issued via an MT700 series to the beneficiary bank and settled through MT780/MT756. Domestically, New Zealand-dollar clearances run over the same ESAS rails for real-time gross settlement (RTGS), while SEPACredit payments are bridged through a participating EEA partner bank that hosts a virtual IBAN for recurring 'pull' disbursements. The treasury suite reserves MT103 as the default rail because it preserves full traceability and meets the AML/CFT 'money trail' expectation of NZ banks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Traded OTC NZD/USD and NZD/AUD FX forwards with tenors up to 12 months, subject to documented underlying treasury exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) covering CNY, INR, IDR and other soft or restricted-convertibility currencies, settled against an independent rate fix and used strictly for hedging export or card-network receivables.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCS) with 6 to 36 month maturity, used to align mismatched asset-and-liability currency bases and to manage balance-sheet interest-rate risk.
Foreign exchange swaps (FX swaps) transacted with licensed New Zealand registered banks for short-term liquidity management across the settlement date.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within one month following the annual return date, which falls on the anniversary of the company's incorporation date (or on the alternate annual return date approved by the Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late filing fee of approximately USD 36 (NZD 60) is imposed; if the return remains outstanding beyond 28 days after the due date, the Registrar may issue infringement notices, and continued default for one or more years allows the Registrar to initiate administrative strike-off, which extinguishes the company's legal capacity and vests its assets in the Crown

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements and Annual Report (FMC Reporting Entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, MBIE, with electronic transmission via the Financial Markets Authority (FMA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the company's balance date (standard balance date is 31 March; alternative balance dates require Registrar approval); the annual report must also be filed with the FMA within four months of the balance date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deliver audited financial statements within the statutory window constitutes an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; the FMA may issue formal warnings, impose civil penalties of up to USD 300,000 (NZD 500,000) against the company and up to USD 30,000 (NZD 50,000) against each director, and may apply to the court for the company's winding-up on the grounds of insolvent or non-compliant administration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA), Financial Service Providers Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 November (or the next business day if 30 November falls on a weekend or public holiday)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-completion within the prescribed period results in automatic removal from the Financial Service Providers Register; FSP registration is a legal precondition for providing financial services in New Zealand, and acting without it exposes the company to criminal liability, fines of up to USD 30,000 (NZD 50,000), and disqualification of directors

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent annual audit applies without size exemption: (1) the entity is a licensed financial institution supervised by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand and the FMA, and (2) the company is an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013. Under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, an FMC reporting entity must be audited every financial year regardless of revenue or asset thresholds; additionally, any New Zealand company that is not 'small' — being an entity with total revenue exceeding USD 18 million (NZD 30 million) and total assets exceeding USD 36 million (NZD 60 million) — is also subject to compulsory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Equivalents to International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS) as issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB) for FMC reporting entities; for balance dates beginning on or after 1 January 2024, the entity shall apply NZ IFRS with the requirement, under Financial Reporting Standard 44, to present its statutory financial statements in accordance with Tier 1 for-profit accounting requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies Act 1993, the company must update its register of members within 10 business days of any share transfer or allotment. The Annual Return filed with the Registrar constitutes the annual statutory confirmation of current shareholding and director details, and all changes must be accurate as at the annual return date. In parallel, the company, as a licensed financial institution under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, must conduct a risk-based annual review of beneficial ownership information as part of its customer due diligence programme; significant transfers of shareholding during the year trigger immediate re-verification of beneficial ownership, with records retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends and the same seven-year statutory record retention period applying to the foundational corporate records.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% (Income Tax Act 2007, Schedule 1, Part A — company rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general corporate tax holidays in New Zealand. Principal rate reliefs: (1) refundable Research and Development Tax Credit of 15% of eligible R&D expenditure (Taxation (Research and Development Tax Credits) Act 2019); (2) imputation credit system eliminating double taxation on resident shareholders of distributed profits (28% imputation credits attach to dividends); (3) tax loss carry-forward with no time limit subject to the 49% ownership continuity test (s IA 5); (4) Covid-era one-year loss carry-back (NZD 5 million cap) was temporary and is no longer generally available; (5) depreciation and fixed-life intangibles deductions apply to digital infrastructure; (6) no patent box or notional interest deduction exists for EMIs.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited / no statutory time limit (must satisfy the ≥49% shareholder continuity of voting and market value test under s IA 5 Income Tax Act 2007)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR4 (Company Income Tax Return); filed electronically via Inland Revenue's myIR portal or through IR-approved tax software (tax agent e-filing). Non-resident companies carrying on business in NZ through a fixed establishment must file the IR4 rather than a non-resident simplified form.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual — one return per income year. Standard balance date: 31 March; substituted financial years require IR approval.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For the standard tax year ending 31 March YYYY: return due 7 July YYYY+1 (non-agent) or 31 March YYYY+2 (registered tax agent). Terminal tax due 7 February YYYY+2 (non-agent) or 7 April YYYY+2 (tax agent). Provisional tax instalments fall due on 7 May YYYY, 7 September YYYY and 7 January YYYY+1, unless the GST-ratio or AIM payment option is adopted. Substituted balance dates shift each due date proportionately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income: gross assessable income of the company for the income year, including EMI service fees, interchange/network fees, float investment interest and foreign-sourced income attributable to the NZ business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income derived from sources in New Zealand or from a business carried on through a fixed establishment/PE in New Zealand; income subject to final NRWT (interest/dividends/royalties) is generally excluded from the IR4 income computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses: deductible expenditure incurred in producing assessable income (s DA 1), excluding capital items, non-deductible entertainment, fines, and expenses of exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses that are both incurred in deriving the NZ assessable income and consistent with arm's-length transfer pricing; head-office overhead allocations must be supported by a documented cost-pool allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income or loss: Box 1 less Box 2, before deduction of tax losses and before offset of subvention payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If Box 3 is a loss, the non-resident must still file the return when required; the loss may be carried forward only if the NZ-resident continuity rules and s IA 5 requirements are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward and deducted: quantum of previously verified net losses offset against current-year net income (subject to the 49% continuity test and the business match test).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident company, losses are recognised only if derived through the NZ PE and can only be used in subsequent NZ PE years; the same continuity of ownership in the loss company must be maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income: Box 3 minus Box 4; this is the amount to which the 28% company rate is applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax is charged on NZ-sourced PE profit at 28%; a non-resident company is not taxed in NZ on non-NZ-sourced income unless it is attributable to the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable on net taxable income (28%, subject to any rebate or special rate).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company's only NZ income is passive (dividends, interest, royalties), the IR4 is not normally used — such income is subject to final NRWT and the company is not required to file an IR4 unless it has a PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: provisional tax paid, resident withholding tax (RWT) credits, foreign tax credits, and imputation credits attached to dividends received.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies may credit NRWT/AIL paid on NZ-source passive income against income tax only if such income is progressively assessed; otherwise the NRWT is final and no credit is claimable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual tax due or refund: Box 6 minus Box 7; if positive, terminal tax is payable by the statutory terminal tax date; if negative, a refund is processed after the annual return is filed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any residual refund is generally paid only to the NZ bank account of the company; refunds to non-resident companies require provision of a TRC and, for treaty purposes, confirmation of beneficial ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credit account (ICA): opening balance, credits (income tax paid), debits (dividends credited), and closing debit balance per the company's imputation return (IR4J where separate format applies).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Imputation credits attached to a dividend paid to a non-resident shareholder do not reduce NRWT; they may form part of the NRWT gross-up base, so the ICA reconciliation must distinguish resident vs non-resident dividend payments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: NZD 250 late-filing penalty under s 139A Tax Administration Act 1994, increased by NZD 250 for each whole month or part month the IR4 remains unfiled. Late payment: 1% late-payment penalty immediately on the due date, a further 4% if unpaid 7 days after the due date, and 1% per month thereafter (s 139B TAA). Use-of-money interest under s 120 TAA accrues daily on unpaid terminal/provisional tax at the prescribed rate (underpayment rate approximately 10-11% p.a. in the 2025 rate cycle). Evasion offences under s 143B expose the company and officers to a fine of up to NZD 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.
